extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of art and literary criticism; art historians, painters, poets, and educated general readers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts evaluative principles for Renaissance painting (especially Giorgione and the Venetian school) and for French Renaissance poetry (the Pleiad/Du Bellay and Ronsard), focusing on subject choice, form, musicality, execution, attribution, and language practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of subject suited to pictorial form
rubrics_metrics.description: A dexterous choice of that subject, or phase of subject; such choice is one of the secrets of Giorgione's school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer matter that 'lends itself most readily and entirely to pictorial form, to complete expression by drawing and colour.' The school favors painted idylls and small 'phases' rather than full articulated narratives; choose a moment or aspect that painting can express wholly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordination of mere subject to pictorial design
rubrics_metrics.description: The subordination of mere subject to pictorial design, to the main purpose of a picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subject should be subordinated to composition and design—the picture's formal needs take precedence over a literal or elaborate story. Giorgione exemplifies selecting phases of subject to serve pictorial unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspiration to musical condition — identification of matter and form
rubrics_metrics.description: An aspiration of all the arts towards music, towards the perfect identification of matter and form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a unity between what is represented (matter) and how it is represented (form) analogous to music's perfect identification; treat painting as aspiring to musical coherence and rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture of instantaneous motion and passing expression (il fuoco Giorgionesco)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution, ease and quickness with which instantaneous motion is reproduced; 'The sudden act, the rapid transition of thought, the passing expression--this he arrests with that vivacity ... il fuoco Giorgionesco.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize brief, vivid actions or expressions (e.g., lacing on armour, a fainting lady, an embrace) that crystallize a moment; technical execution should convey immediacy and life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of 'ideal instants' that condense long histories
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting a single, profoundly significant instant—a gesture, look or smile—into which all past and future condense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose and render moments that imply a larger narrative or history without explicating it; dramatic economy and implication are virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of music and music-like subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: The perfect moments of music itself, the making or hearing of music, are prominent as subjects; life conceived as listening or music-like intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Music, tuning, listening, and music-associated gestures are favored subject-matters because they naturally admit pictorial rhythm and mood; use sound-related motifs to evoke mood and temporal depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence and depiction of water and its effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence of water—the well, marble-rimmed pool, pouring or drawing of water—is characteristic and suggestive in this school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include wells, pools, flowing water, and its acoustic/visual effects (coolness, reflection, freshness) as compositional and symbolic devices (example: Fete Champetre). Depict water to enrich atmosphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonious balance between figure and landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: A balance, a modulated unison of landscape and persons, so that neither personage nor scenery is ever a mere pretext for the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose so figures and landscape mutually enfold each other; avoid treating background as mere backdrop or figures as isolated foreground elements (example: Jacob embracing Rachel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmosphere: liquid, empyrean air and refined colour
rubrics_metrics.description: Air seeming vivid and empyrean; colour spun like 'gold dust' through flesh and objects; clarity and purity of atmosphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a refined, luminous atmosphere—clear, pure air, subtle colour harmonies (golden filaments, 'liquid air') that unify figures and setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intimacy and format: cabinet or 'portable' pictures
rubrics_metrics.description: Small groups or spaces detached and framed so they may be moved, like a poem in manuscript, to live with the viewer in a cabinet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor compositions and scales suited to private, contemplative viewing (cabinet pictures); design works to function as intimate, transportable objects for prolonged personal enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tact in choosing scenes of play, masque, and 'listening' moments
rubrics_metrics.description: The school selects moments of play, masques, dressing-up, listening—exquisite pauses in time—where play allows freer passage to happier powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select playful, disguised, or receptive moments—masques, musical listening, games—that reveal refined human moods and allow painterly invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'park' scenery and refined rustic accessories
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenery akin to 'park scenery'—grouped trees, deftly economised undulations, rustic buildings refined into elegant features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose landscapes with cultivated, harmonious rural elements (park-like layouts) and tasteful rustic architecture to provide graceful surroundings for figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of authenticity/genuine work: sustained evenness of perfection
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'distinction' of the Concert (Pitti) — its sustained evenness of perfection in design, execution, and choice of personal type — becomes the standard of Giorgione's genuine work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent excellence across design, execution, and typology as a criterion for attributing works to a master; inconsistencies suggest imitation or different authorship (the 'new Vasari' approach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of indirect influence and the 'vraie verité'
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond strictly ascertained facts, take note of the indirect influence by which an artist enlarges his permanent efficacy—the 'vraie verite' supplementing narrow facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating an artist, include cultural influence, traditions, copies, and the school generated around a reputed figure; do not reduce assessment to authenticated works alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate the native language rather than rely on dead languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleads for illustration and ennobling of the French language—to use the mother-tongue for the fullest moving and passionate expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor writing poetry and prose in one's living language to achieve immediacy and passion; do not cede literary thought solely to Greek or Latin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations cannot fully teach ornament or naturalness
rubrics_metrics.description: One cannot learn the right use of figures and ornament from translations because each language has peculiarities; forced translations become constrained and cold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat translations as imperfect models for stylistic devices; rely on native-language practice to develop idiomatic ornamentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of good translation: reproduce the same affections
rubrics_metrics.description: The test: read Demosthenes and Homer in Latin, Cicero and Virgil in French, and see whether they produce in you the same affections as in the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge translations by their emotional and aesthetic equivalence to originals rather than literal fidelity alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elegance, daintiness and nicety of execution
rubrics_metrics.description: A characteristic 'nicety, a remarkable daintiness of hand'—a 'nettete remarquable d'execution'—applies to French art and poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value delicate, precise execution, refined line and surface detail (in painting) and polished, elegant phrasing (in poetry) as central virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to musicality and varied metre in poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Ronsard gave structure and taught a changefulness and variety of metre which keep the curiosity always excited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In poetry, use formal innovations (strophe/antistrophe, meter variation) to sustain interest and produce a pleasing page-aspect; musical quality matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write for a refined, courtly, erudite audience when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry of the Pleiad is 'poetry not for the people, but for a confined circle, for courtiers, great lords and erudite persons.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match tone, learned references, and mannered elegance to a cultivated audience; recognize when work is deliberately confined in scope and social function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of distinctive style and manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything that has style, that has been done as no other man or age could have done it, has its true value and interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize authentic, characteristic manner over mere neutrality; uniqueness of style confers lasting aesthetic value even when fashions change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learnedness, pedantry and classical orthographic care as visible features
rubrics_metrics.description: Anxiety about orthography, the letter e Grecque, true spelling of Latin names, use of Greek words and even coined terms—a pedantic learnedness in Ronsard's circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize classical pedantry and classical borrowings as deliberate stylistic choices (charm or fault depending on taste); technical correctness and classical allusion were signs of cultivated status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refinement by blending native taste with foreign finesse
rubrics_metrics.description: French Renaissance is not wholesale importation from Italy but a phase of native Gothic refined by Italian ornament—blending Italian finesse with Northern design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage selective assimilation: adopt useful foreign refinements while preserving native characteristics; value synthesis that yields a new, graceful phase rather than mere imitation.
